summary: Built 1934 in Lassen National Forest; last used as a lookout in 2007 and called unsafe for use; a 2020 project moved its radio gear to a container.

facts.design: California Region 5 Plan BC-301 cabin on an enclosed timber tower
facts.status_note: Still standing, but the register's text dates from CAL FIRE's 2011-2012 plan and calls the building unsafe for use

access.note: The register and the 2011-2012 CAL FIRE plan call the building unsafe for use; that is not a formal closure, and no current opening or closure notice was found

visit.trail_note: No public route described in the sources read; the register calls the building unsafe for use

facts.agency: US Forest Service - Lassen National Forest

events.note: Register gives 1934; Forest Lookouts says a Conservation Corps crew erected the lookout that year
High winds tore the west shutters off in June 1937
September 1937 fire, started by a spark from a flatcar's brake shoe, destroyed a logging trestle over Dry Creek; the Dyer Mountain lookout was first to report it
John and Lillian Dulvick began their tenth summer season at the lookout
Staffed for the 1991 fire season with severity funds, per a 1992 Lassen County Times item
Opened June 15, 1992, funded for two months
Register says the tower has not been used as a lookout since 2007
CAL FIRE 2011-2012 plan update: building unsafe, not staffed, Forest Service might pursue demolition; removed from CAL FIRE's list of historic buildings to preserve
Decision signed November 7, 2020 for a new special use permit to move CAL FIRE radio equipment from the lookout into a 10 by 10 foot container; project marked completed

resolved_conflicts.explanation: A 1992 item ties the first budget cut to the 1991-92 fiscal year, and an October 1996 item still calls the lookout state funded. The register quotes CAL FIRE's 2011-2012 plan dating the permanent cut to about 15 years before the plan. The story reports these dates and gives no single end date.

notes_for_editor: Height left out: the register's '15 foot enclosed timber tower' may mean the tower or the cab, so the record's height_m stays null. Access was 'closed' and is now 'unknown': the register's 'unsafe for use' wording is not a closure notice, and no current Forest Service or CAL FIRE notice was found, so check with Lassen National Forest before stating access. The register text is from the 2011-2012 plan, and the newest source is the 2020 project page, so the current condition is unverified. The dyermtn.com resort site describes a separate resort proposal on the mountain and is not used. No new photos. Build year 1934 agrees across both sources.
